sn45.2:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans where there was a town of the Sakyans named Nagaraka.
sn45.2:1.3: Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side, and said to him:
sn45.2:1.4: “Venerable sir, this is half of the holy life, that is, good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship.”
sn45.2:2.2: This is the entire holy life, Ānanda, that is, good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship.
sn45.2:2.3: When a bhikkhu has a good friend, a good companion, a good comrade, it is to be expected that he will develop and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path.
sn45.2:3.1: “And how, Ānanda, does a bhikkhu who has a good friend, a good companion, a good comrade, develop and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path?
sn45.2:3.2: Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu develops right view, which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, maturing in release.
sn45.2:3.9: right concentration, which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, maturing in release.
sn45.2:3.10: It is in this way, Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who has a good friend, a good companion, a good comrade, develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path.
sn45.2:4.1: “By the following method too, Ānanda, it may be understood how the entire holy life is good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship:
sn45.2:4.2: by relying upon me as a good friend, Ānanda, beings subject to birth are freed from birth; beings subject to aging are freed from aging; beings subject to death are freed from death; beings subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair are freed from sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair.
sn45.2:4.3: By this method, Ānanda, it may be understood how the entire holy life is good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship.”
